title: fix: CVE-2026-112366 prevent ReDoS in single-branch repeated extglobs
body:
## Summary
Fixes [GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf) / CVE-2026-112366.

`analyzeRepeatedExtglob` skipped single-branch repeated extglobs such as `+(*)` or `+(*a)`, so they compiled to nested unbounded quantifiers (e.g. `(?:[^/]*?a)+`), causing exponential backtracking on short inputs.

## Fix
A single branch containing a top-level `*` (with no `/`, groups, alternation, nested extglobs or globstar) absorbs its own repetition, so:

- `+(P)` → `(?:P)`
- `*(P)` → `(?:P)?`

These are semantically equivalent and remove the nested quantifier. Other cases keep the existing risky-extglob handling. The rewrite is skipped when `maxExtglobRecursion: false`.

| Pattern | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `+(*a)` | `(?:[^/]*?a)+` | `(?:[^/]*?a)` |
| `*(*a)` | `(?:[^/]*?a)*` | `(?:[^/]*?a)?` |

Before the fix, matching `'a'.repeat(24) + 'b'` against `+(*a)` took ~107ms and doubled with each extra char. With the fix it takes ~0ms.

## Tests
Added cases in `test/options.maxExtglobRecursion.js` covering:
- no nested quantifiers in the generated regex
- a timing bound on malicious input
- matching semantics preserved (`+(*)c`, `+(*a)`, `+(a*b)`, `*(*.js)`)

All 1999 tests pass.
